title: Slow computer & freezes
blurb: Slow, frozen, fan loud, high CPU or memory, apps not responding.

remedies.title: Computer is slow
remedies.why: Usually too much running at once, a nearly full disk, startup apps, updates working in the background, or not having restarted for weeks.

steps.text: Restart the computer (a real restart). Fast startup on Windows means Shut down isn't a fresh start.
Run the Health check: it flags low disk space, memory pressure and other common causes.
See what's busy: Task Manager › Processes › sort by CPU, Memory and Disk.
See what's busy: Activity Monitor › CPU and Memory (watch Memory Pressure).
Free up disk space if under ~10% is left.
Turn off startup apps you don't need.
Turn off login items you don't need.
Close browser tabs and quit apps you're not using.

remedies.escalate: If it's still slow with little running, tell IT the Health check result and how much memory the computer has.

remedies.title: Computer froze completely
remedies.why: One app is blocking the screen, the desktop shell hung, or (rarely) the whole system stopped.

steps.text: Wait a minute; heavy work can stall it briefly.
Press Ctrl+Alt+Delete › Task Manager, select the app that's Not responding › End task.
If the taskbar and Start menu froze, restart Explorer.
Press ⌘+Option+Esc, choose the app › Force Quit.
If nothing reacts, hold the power button ~10 seconds to turn it off, wait, turn it on. Unsaved work will be lost.
If it happens often, look at Reliability Monitor for the app or driver behind it.

remedies.title: An app says "Not responding" or won't close
remedies.why: The app is stuck waiting (on the network, a file, or a dialog hidden behind another window) or crashed.

steps.text: Look for a hidden dialog: Alt+Tab (⌘+Tab) through windows; one may be waiting for an answer.
End it in Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) › select › End task.
Force Quit with ⌘+Option+Esc, or in Activity Monitor.
Update the app; if it keeps freezing, reinstall it.

remedies.title: CPU at 100%, fan loud, computer hot
remedies.why: A process is working hard (updates, antivirus scan, indexing, a runaway browser tab), or dust blocks cooling.

steps.text: Find the process: Task Manager › Processes › sort by CPU.
Find the process: Activity Monitor › CPU › sort by % CPU.
Windows Update, antivirus scans and Search indexing calm down on their own after a while, especially right after starting.
Close the busy app or browser tab; if it's always the same app, update or reinstall it.
Use the laptop on a hard surface (not a bed or lap) so air can flow; vents can be cleaned with compressed air.

remedies.escalate: If an unknown process uses the CPU all the time, tell IT its name (it may be unwanted software).

remedies.title: Memory (RAM) is always full
symptoms: your system has run out of application memory
remedies.why: Many browser tabs and big apps fill memory; once it's full, the computer swaps to disk and slows down.

steps.text: See what uses memory: Task Manager › sort by Memory.
Check Memory Pressure in Activity Monitor › Memory (green is fine, red means too little memory).
Close unused tabs and apps; turn on the browser's memory saver.
Restart once in a while; it clears leaks.
Computers with 8 GB struggle with today's apps; 16 GB is comfortable.

remedies.title: Disk at 100% in Task Manager
remedies.why: Updates, Search indexing, antivirus, or a slow old hard drive (not SSD) that can't keep up.

steps.text: Wait 15–20 minutes after starting; background tasks often finish.
See which process: Task Manager › sort by Disk, or Resource Monitor › Disk.
Check free space; a nearly full disk makes it worse.
Check the disk's health in DeskMedic's Disks page.
A computer with a spinning hard drive gets much faster with an SSD.

remedies.title: Many different apps crash
remedies.why: When many apps crash, the cause is shared: damaged system files, failing memory, a bad driver, or security software.

steps.text: Install all updates.
Install all updates.
Repair Windows system files.
Repair the Windows image if the file check found problems it couldn't fix.
Test the memory (restarts the PC).
Look at crash history in Reliability Monitor.
Run Apple Diagnostics: shut down, then hold the power button (Apple silicon) and press ⌘D at the options screen.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT the names of the apps and the crash times; Reliability Monitor's details help.

remedies.title: Taskbar, Start menu or desktop frozen or blank
remedies.why: Explorer (which draws the taskbar, Start and desktop) hung or crashed.

steps.text: Restart Explorer (open windows stay; the taskbar comes back).
If icons show blank or wrong pictures, rebuild the icon cache.
Repair system files if it keeps happening.
